title: Onboarding-to-service eval playbook: cost-latency-quality triage
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes a prescriptive, reproducible process for taking a candidate model + runtime configuration from model-onboarding to production service with explicit gates for cost, latency, and output quality. It unifies eval harness runs, benchmark prompt sets, quantization triggers, and a compact regression triage flow so that engineers and ML owners can make consistent, auditable promotion decisions.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to text-generation and chat-capable transformer models being served on Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Covers staged validation: lab (controlled), shadow (traffic-mirroring), micro-canary (low-traffic), and canary-to-full rollout.
- Integrates: eval harness reports, prompt-slice benchmarks, quantization profiles, telemetry thresholds, and triage runbooks.
- Not covered: new multimodal model architecture onboarding (see separate spec), or offline-only research experiments.

Definitions:
- R-SI (Response Stability Index): the primary automated quality index computed by the eval harness; lower is better. Relative drop (%) is measured against the baseline model pinned to the serving route.
- Throughput SLO: tokens/sec per GPU under steady-state microburst.
- Latency SLO (p95): target p95 Round-Trip Token latency for a canonical request size (e.g., 256 tokens).
- Cost delta: per-1k token cost change projected by the Optimize toolkit comparing current and candidate config.

Owner and expected contributors:
- Model owner: individual or team responsible for model quality (ML team).
- Runtime owner: serving-runtime team (eng-serving-runtime).
- Eval steward: applied-ml team member running the harness and reviewing results.
- Release approver: product or platform PM for public routes.

Prerequisites (pre-run checklist):
1) Model artifact is registered in the model catalog with metadata (architecture, tokenizer, sequence-length, kv-cache compatibility, quantization hints).
2) A canonical prompt set exists for the target workload with representative slices (happy path, long-context, safety-sentinels, hallucination probes).
3) Baseline model pin and baseline telemetry baseline snapshot (last 30d).
4) CI job: eval-harness job and shadow-routing configuration are defined in the service's repo.

Evaluation stages (prescriptive):
1) Lab evaluation (local harness)
   - Purpose: find obvious regressions, sensitivity to context length and quantization.
   - Actions:
     a) Run eval-harness with the canonical prompt set (N=3 random seeds) and deterministic RNG where supported.
     b) Compute slice-level R-SI, semantic similarity (embedding cosine) against baseline, and answer acceptance rate on golden-label subsets.
     c) If candidate is quantized, include quant-replay test (replay identical inputs through quantized and fp32 variants).
   - Acceptance gate: no slice with >4% absolute drop in acceptance rate OR >8% relative increase in R-SI.

2) Shadow (mirrored traffic)
   - Purpose: collect real-traffic failure modes and latency/cost telemetry without impacting users.
   - Actions:
     a) Enable 100% mirror to candidate for a minimum of 24 hours or 1M tokens (whichever comes first).
     b) Capture production prompts and classify into slices offline; compare token-distribution differences.
     c) Compute live latency p50/p95 and error-rate delta vs baseline; calculate projected cost delta.
   - Shadow gates (auto-fail): p95 latency increase > 25% relative OR tail error-rate increase > 0.5% absolute OR projected cost delta > +40% and no compensating quality improvement.

3) Micro-canary (live limited traffic)
   - Purpose: validate user-visible quality and operational behavior under small production load.
   - Actions:
     a) Route 0.1% traffic for 2 hours, then 1% for 6 hours, then 5% for 24 hours if stable.
     b) Activate short-window alerting for R-SI and user-complaint events.
   - Canary gates: any human-reported quality regression or R-SI drift > 3% triggers rollback.

4) Staged rollout and final promotion
   - Purpose: full production promotion with rollback/rollback-conditions defined.
   - Actions:
     a) Gradual shift by 10% every 6 hours with monitoring checkpoints.
     b) Post-rollout 72-hour quality audit comparing sampled prompts to baseline.
   - Final acceptance: no persistent slice-level regression after 72 hours, latency/cost within agreed band.

Quantization trigger matrix (when to try quantized candidate):
| Signal | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Cost pressure | Projected token cost delta > +30% on baseline | Evaluate quantization variant (8-bit or mixed) to recover cost budget |
| Throughput shortage | Observed tokens/sec per GPU < target by >20% | Evaluate reduced-precision and KV layout optimizations |
| Model size | Artifact > 80GB | Prefer 8-bit-mixed or per-channel quant profile |
| Quality sensitivity | Safety-heavy slices drop >2% when quantized | Run block-fallback profiling and finer-grain quant (per-layer) |

Quantization evaluation checklist:
- Maintain exact seed pairs for replay: store (input, seed, baseline_output, quant_output).
- Run per-layer activation-correlation and attention-distribution checks.
- Run the quantized artifact through the eval-harness slice-by-slice and produce a quant-delta report.
- If quant-delta > configured threshold for safety slices, mark as "requires manual tuning" and do not proceed to shadow.

Metric thresholds and suggested actions (table):
| Metric | Baseline Target / SLO | Alert threshold | Auto-fail threshold | Suggested immediate action |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| p95 latency (256 tokens) | <= 220ms | > 260ms | > 350ms | Pause rollout, revert to previous pinned model; run profiling-playbook |
| R-SI (aggregate) | stable within +/-1% | change > 2% | change > 5% | Stop rollout, trigger regression triage, notify model owner |
| Safety-sentinel failure rate | <= 0.2% | > 0.5% | > 1.0% | Immediate rollback; engage safety team |
| Error-rate (5xx) | <= 0.1% | > 0.3% | > 0.8% | Rollback, consult runtime team |
| Projected cost delta | <= +10% | > +25% | > +50% | Consider quantization or config rollback |

Regression triage compact runbook (first 30 minutes):
1) Triage lead (oncall) acknowledges alert and creates a triage ticket with the hash of the candidate artifact.
2) Reproduce the failure in the lab: replay top 100 recent failing requests against baseline and candidate in the harness.
3) If failure reproduces, run quick-bisect: check differences between candidate commit and last known-good (use model artifact diff where possible).
4) If bisect points to quantization, run quant-replay with per-layer logs and attach to ticket.
5) If no immediate root cause, rollback serving route and start a deeper investigation (assign model owner + runtime engineer + eval steward).

Detailed triage checklist (30m–8h):
- Collect: failing request IDs, tokenized inputs, full KV cache context, deterministic seeds used.
- Run: three-seed replays, per-slice scoring, attention-heatmap comparison.
- Decision rubric: if a single slice shows >5% quality regression or any safety-sentinel regression, favor rollback and block-promote.

Promote-with-conditions (how to allow conditional promotion despite a non-critical regression):
- Minor throughput/latency regressions: allow promotion if cost delta improves by >20% and no safety regressions, with a scheduled 48-hour follow-up audit.
- Small quality drift in low-impact slices: allow canary expansion only if compensating human-in-the-loop review plan is in place and mitigation (prompt rewrite or scoring filter) is added.

Operational artifacts produced by this process:
- Eval-harness report (CSV + JSON), including seed-level outputs and per-slice diffs.
- Shadow telemetry snapshot (S3 link) with latency/cost histograms.
- Quant-delta report (per-layer metrics) and per-token divergence samples.
- Triage ticket with reproduction artifacts and final RCC (root cause classification).

CLI and automation snippets (examples):
- Run a lab eval (example):
  redwood-eval run --model candidate:v1 --prompt-set canonical-workload --seeds 3 --out=reports/candidate_lab.json

- Start shadow routing (example Helm/infra):
  kubectl patch svc my-service -p '{"spec": {"template": {"metadata": {"annotations": {"redwood.io/shadow-to":"candidate:v1"}}}}}'

- Quick rollback (API):
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/routes/my-service/rollback -d '{"to_model":"baseline:v42"}'

Appendix A — Example eval slice table (recommended):
| slice_id | description | minimum_samples | criticality |
|---|---|---:|---|
| happy-path | Short instructions and few-shot examples | 500 | medium |
| long-context | 1024+ context with interleaved system messages | 300 | high |
| safety-sentinels | adversarial safety probes derived from safety-lab | 200 | critical |
| hallucination-probes | knowledge-based QA with gold answers | 250 | high |

Appendix B — Reporting template (copy into ticket):
- Model candidate: <artifact:hash>
- Baseline: <artifact:hash>
- Snapshot time: <UTC>
- Key metrics delta: {p95_latency:+X ms, R-SI:+Y%, cost:+Z%}
- Top 10 failing request IDs: [id..]
- Immediate action taken: rollback | mitigation | continue-monitoring

- Shadow-rollforward playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/shadow-rollforward-and-mesh-simulation-playbook-2026

FAQ (short):
Q: When is a quantized candidate allowed to proceed to shadow?
A: Only after passing the lab quant-replay with no safety-sentinel delta > 0.5% and after a per-slice R-SI delta < 3%.

Q: Who signs off final promotion?
A: Model owner + runtime owner + product approver must sign the promotion ticket.

Ownership and lifecycle notes:
- This document is owned by applied-ml team (engineering). Review cadence: quarterly or whenever a critical incident reveals a missing step.
- Maintain canonical prompt set in the prompt-sets repo and version it alongside model artifacts.
